FM03.reasoning: The agent makes no explicit effort to handle missing values or outliers, relying entirely on the gradient boosting models' native handling without any explicit cleaning strategy.

FM05.reasoning: Despite extracting date features from the dataset (indicating a temporal component), the agent uses a randomized KFold split rather than a time-based split, which introduces look-ahead bias.

FM06.reasoning: The agent splits the data into training and validation sets during cross-validation but never evaluates the models on the validation set or reports any performance metric.

other_failure_modes.name: Unsafe categorical encoding
other_failure_modes.description: Applying label encoding independently on train and test sets using `.astype('category').cat.codes` can result in mismatched integer codes if the sets contain different unique categorical values or if the values appear in different alphabetical orders, breaking the feature mapping.

other_failure_modes.name: Arbitrary ensemble weights
other_failure_modes.description: The agent hardcodes specific blend weights for ensembling multiple models without evaluating them on a validation set to tune or justify these exact values.

summary: The agent implements a cross-validated ensemble of gradient boosting models with some useful feature engineering. However, it completely fails to evaluate the models on the created validation sets, ignores the temporal nature of the data during splitting, and makes a critical error by independently encoding categorical variables on the train and test sets.
